finalText:
**Merge** keeps both branches visible in your history. It creates a new commit that ties them together. Everyone sees that you merged something in. Your history looks like a tree.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the branch you're catching up to. It rewrites history to make a straight line. It looks like you did all your work after everyone else did theirs.

Use **merge** when the branch is shared or published. If other people are using it, rewriting history breaks their copies. Merge is the safe default.

Use **rebase** on branches only you work on, before you send them for review. It cleans up the story so your commits read clearly without the noise of everyone else's work in between.

The tradeoff: merge is safer but leaves the history messier. Rebase is cleaner but you can only do it on branches nobody else is using. Don't rebase something that other people have already pulled — you'll create duplicate commits and confuse everyone.
